text:
Denton Mateychuk is one of the few things going right in Columbus. The 12th pick in 2022, in his first full season, plays 22 minutes a night and the Blue Jackets take 51% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, almost five points better than when he sits, on a team that's winless in five. He has four goals and seven points in 19 games. Among defensemen drafted 7th to 17th since 2005, the median first full season was 0.24 points a game; he's at 0.37.

He's a defenseman who goes to the net. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 95th percentile for chances from the home-plate area last season, and his own chances this year (0.38 expected goals per 60) are well up from 0.23. The goals are a little ahead of that (12.5% shooting), so expect fewer to go in. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.2 wins last season and 3.2 by expected wins, a sign the chances were there before the goals were. His minutes are down almost two a night over his last 10; whether that's matchups or a message is worth watching.
